![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14274391/assets/a3dfc27c8cae5db8bccd14048366531e2aa556802943d464ea12b1568a8ba380.png)

Which of the diagrams shown above represent subspaces of ${R}^{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
Let's analyze each diagram in turn.

- Diagram I does not represent a subspace. The vector $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ lies inside given subset. But

$$
(-1)\cdot a=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

lies outside the subset.

- Diagram II does not represent a subspace. The vector $a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ lies inside given subset. But

$$
(-1)\cdot a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

lies outside the subset.

- Diagram III does not represent a subspace since in does not contain the zero-vector.

So, the correct answer is "None".
